title: Silas and the Horizon
premise: Gideon Brightwater smuggles memories in the silence between the Meridian Fleet and the Cryo Ark, two halves of a sundered humanity whose truce expires in ninety days. When a distress beacon transmits in Old Terran — a language extinct since the Severance — Gideon follows it to a drifting ship where the Ark's first sleepers are waking decades early, their memories harvested by someone desperate to prove the Ark's founding was a lie. With the fleet closing in and the Ark's council demanding the sleepers stay frozen, Gideon must smuggle the truth itself: the memories proving both halves committed the same crime. In the end, Gideon broadcasts the shared past to both fleets, the truce dissolves into a harder, honest negotiation, and Gideon — half-fleet, half-Ark by blood — chooses neither side, staying with the wakers on the drifting ship that becomes humanity's first neutral ground.
about_author: Paloma Lockridge is a former radio archivist who spent a decade restoring dead broadcasts from the early spaceflight era, an obsession that bleeds into every story she tells. She writes from a converted lighthouse on the northern coast, where she claims the fog helps her hear what her characters are trying not to say.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: Gideon Brightwater runs a memory consignment past Meridian customs, hiding grief-recordings inside shipping manifests. POV: Gideon. Establishes the smuggling trade, the fleet's surveillance state, and Gideon's own half-erased childhood. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Between worlds, Gideon's copilot Wren patches the ship and argues about taking the safe lane versus the long route through the Silent Reach. POV: Gideon. We learn the Ark and Fleet haven't spoken in two centuries and the truce expires soon. Emotional beat: restless anticipation before the break.

chapters.title: A Language With No Speakers
chapters.summary: A distress signal arrives in Old Terran, extinct since the Severance. Gideon, who carries a forbidden fragment of the language in a smuggled memory, recognizes it. POV: Gideon, with Wren skeptical. Emotional beat: the shock of hearing a dead tongue call your name.

chapters.title: Into the Silent Reach
chapters.summary: Against Wren's protest, Gideon diverts to the signal's origin. Customs drones shadow them, forcing a desperate burn through a debris field. POV: Wren, revealing their loyalty and fear. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into commitment.

chapters.title: The Drifting Womb
chapters.summary: They board a derelict Ark seed-ship: rows of cryopods, half open, their sleepers missing. A single survivor, an old woman named Iva, greets them in broken Old Terran. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: haunted awe at a tomb that is also a nursery.

chapters.title: What Iva Remembered
chapters.summary: Iva reveals she is a memory-keeper who woke early to guard the sleepers' extracted memories, stored in the ship's core. Someone has been stealing them. POV: Iva flashback woven with Gideon's present. Emotional beat: grief for a history no one was allowed to keep.

chapters.title: The Thief in the Ice
chapters.summary: Gideon traces the memory thefts to a saboteur still in cryosleep — a Fleet archivist embedded in the Ark's founding generation. Waking him risks everything. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing the past is still being fought over.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: A Fleet patrol hails them; Gideon bluffs passage while learning the truce expires in ninety days, after which the Fleet may claim the Ark by force. POV: Wren, monitoring the negotiation. Emotional beat: a clock starting in the chest.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Confession
chapters.summary: Revived, the archivist Dain Marrow admits the Fleet ordered the memory thefts to erase evidence of a shared atrocity — the Severance was mutual betrayal, not Ark treachery. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: guilt offered like a wound, asking to be believed.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Gideon transmits to the Ark council, who demand the sleepers stay frozen and the memories destroyed to preserve the peace. The council offers Gideon citizenship — and erasure of their smuggler past. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: belonging dangled like a bribe.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren, born Fleet, confronts their own indoctrination and chooses to stay with Gideon, burning their Fleet credentials. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: love declared not in words but in a sacrificed identity.

chapters.title: The Memory Vault
chapters.summary: Gideon and Iva open the vault and experience the founding memories: both Fleet and Ark ordered the same massacre, each blaming the other for two centuries. POV: Gideon inside the memory. Emotional beat: horror and a terrible, liberating symmetry.

chapters.title: Customs Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Fleet customs boards the seed-ship on a warrant Gideon's old handler sold them. A firefight in the cryo-bay risks the sleeping thousands. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: terror that survival might cost the very lives they came to save.

chapters.title: The Handler's Price
chapters.summary: Gideon's former handler, Sef, offers to bury the warrant if Gideon hands over the vault — Sef intends to sell the truth back to both sides as leverage. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: the seduction of the old life, and its rot.

chapters.title: What Survival Is Worth
chapters.summary: Iva, dying, tells Gideon the Ark's founders chose memory-keepers precisely for this moment — someone had to carry the truth across the silence. POV: Iva. Emotional beat: a torch passed with the last of her strength.

chapters.title: The Truce Expires
chapters.summary: The ninety days end. Fleet warships and Ark defense drones face each other over the seed-ship while Gideon's crew is trapped between. POV: Wren on the bridge. Emotional beat: the held breath of a civilization deciding.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Gideon hijacks both fleets' comm arrays and broadcasts the founding memories in the raw — Old Terran included — forcing every ship to witness the shared crime at once. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: the climax; truth as the only weapon left, fired at everyone.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: The fleets don't reconcile — they stall, furious and shaken, while their crews demand answers. Dain defects to Gideon's side, bringing Fleet archives that corroborate the broadcast. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: aftermath as vertigo; no going back.

chapters.title: Negotiation at the Womb
chapters.summary: Both sides send envoys to the neutral seed-ship. Gideon, the only person trusted by neither and needed by both, brokers the first talks — starting with waking the sleepers in shifts, half from each lineage. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: exhausted, imperfect hope.

chapters.title: The Waking
chapters.summary: The first sleepers wake to a world that has finally told them the truth. One of them is Gideon's grandmother, whose memory fragment Gideon has carried since chapter one — she completes it. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: grief and reunion braided into one.

chapters.title: Which Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: The Ark and Fleet sign a provisional accord, neither surrendering, both changed. Gideon is offered command of the new joint customs authority — the smuggler asked to police the border they spent their life crossing. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the price of survival, paid and counted.

chapters.title: The Horizon, Kept
chapters.summary: Gideon declines the post, keeping the seed-ship as neutral ground and a school for the waking. Wren stays; the long route becomes a ferry line between two worlds learning to speak. POV: Gideon, closing. Emotional beat: belonging found not in a side, but in the space between.
